territorial_scope.description: Applies to exports, reexports and in-country transfers of covered integrated circuits to entities located or headquartered in countries of concern named in the section.

evidence.quote: shall require a license for the export, reexport, or in-country transfer of a covered integrated circuit

summary.short: If enacted, adds ECRA section 1758A requiring a Commerce license for exports, reexports and in-country transfers of covered integrated circuits to entities in listed countries of concern, with a trusted-US-person exemption, congressional certification, and a temporary license freeze.
summary.long: Amends Part I of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 by inserting section 1758A on exports of covered integrated circuits. Countries of concern include the People's Republic of China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela under the Maduro regime; covered circuits are defined by export classification numbers and performance thresholds, excluding products not designed or marketed for data centers. The Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security must require a license for exports, reexports and in-country transfers of such circuits to entities located or headquartered in a country of concern, and may not issue a general license. Congressional committees must receive the application and specified certifications at least 30 days before approval; no license may issue in that period or if Congress enacts a joint resolution prohibiting the export. Prior licenses for such exports are terminated, and all such licenses are denied until 14 days after the Commerce Secretary submits a national security strategy. Exports of such circuits to non-concern destinations are exempt from EAR sections 742.6 and 744.23 licensing when kept under a designated trusted United States person's control; designation standards are due within 90 days.

notes: Introduced bill text (pending, not enacted). Internal points: (1) Section 1758A(b)(1) requires licences 'Beginning on the date of the enactment of this section', while (f) denies all such licences until 14 days after the national security strategy in (g) is submitted; (g) sets no submission deadline, so the (a)(4)(B) update authority ('18 months after' that submission) and (f) have an undated anchor. (2) Section 1758A(c)(1) requires certification 'Not fewer than 30 days prior' to approving a licence, and (c)(2)(A)(i) bars issuance until 30 days after the committees receive it; both apply together. (3) Section 1758A(a)(6) fixes the Commerce Control List 'as in effect on December 15, 2025'. (4) Section 1758A(d)(2) sets a 90-day regulation deadline; (d)(3) on allied expansion has no deadline. (5) Section 1758A(e) terminates pre-enactment licences without stating a date. Relation targets are US statutes and regulations not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is left empty. The section_status relations field is required by the schema although relation entries are present.
